newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania gets $87.5 million from EIB in road loan.
newsitem.headline: Romania gets $87.5 million from EIB in road loan.

text.p: The European Investment Bank (EIB) has granted a 70 million Ecu (some $87.5 million) loan to Romania for a road rehabilitation project, the Finance Ministry said on Friday.
It said the National Road Administration (AND) would receive the loan, which is part of a $553 million project, the second phase of a broad programme to upgrade Romania's potholed road network.
The second phase aims to continue the rehabilitation of 1,000 km (625 miles) of roads, and the construction of new motorways started in 1993.

The World Bank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development are also participating in the project with $150 million and $85.4 million respectively. Some $75 million will come from the European Union's Phare programme and the rest is funded by the Romanian government, the finance ministry said.
The EIB loan, granted for 20 years at standard terms, would help modernise some 381 km (238 miles) of national roads linking cities in Transylvania in central Romania.

Transport Ministry sources said two-thirds of the total road network of 14,500 km (9,000 miles) are in need of immediate repairs, as are some 900 km (550 miles) of the rail network, which extends over 11,000 km (7,000 miles).
Romania's roads and railways were neglected under the communists and are now further deteriorating due to lack of funds for repairs and growing traffic.
Earlier this month, the Romanian parliament passed a draft law awarding road and railway concessions in a bid to improve the country's infrastructure.
Last year, Romania announced plans to award concessions worth $1.8 billion to foreign investors as part of a broader programme to improve the road network.
Official estimates say Romania needs about $30 billion to repair and develop its road, rail, air and sea transport by the year 2005. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
